### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 33 pages)`, `sharingModel (literal, 43 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5d97dedb89e2a46b2fca531d159f6c6e6d1948ba` — the merge of head `086d6f1adca2add2f9d36ca75ec33b85c6c72786` into base `404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5d97dedb89e2a46b2fca531d159f6c6e6d1948ba && git checkout 5d97dedb89e2a46b2fca531d159f6c6e6d1948ba
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc 086d6f1adca2add2f9d36ca75ec33b85c6c72786 && git checkout -B drift-repro 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc && git merge --no-ff 086d6f1adca2add2f9d36ca75ec33b85c6c72786

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `af10b608d3d36109b04104a2f9450eddbf4de2e7`
Local-runs: none

Read: cards #23269, #23270, #23271 with every comment (triage `6147340022` / `6147368827` / `6147391920`, the cloud addendum `6147404577`, the claims, report `6152379792`, ACCEPT `6152456700`); PR #23315 body, its one bot comment, the 17-file list and the net diff `origin/main...af10b608d` (+1079 / -59, identical to the file list); #23100, #23160 and PR #23179 as the predecessor shapes; `origin/main` for ADR-0087, the conversions registry, `contracts/automation-service.ts`, `metadata-protocol`'s `protocol.ts` and `stored-migration.ts`, `service-automation`'s `engine.ts`, the walk helpers, the value-slot judge and the three D3 entries; the head's check-runs (two polls, 18:3xZ and 18:45Z).

**Check-runs on the head at 18:45Z: 40 runs, 29 success, 5 skipped, 6 `in_progress` (Test Core 1 to 6).** `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness` and the claim guards are green. The six Test Core shards are reported as still running, not assumed.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong.

1. **One fate per card, refused and listed, under triage's rule (D2 only where lossless; otherwise refused and listed; ⛔ no runtime tolerance): RIGHT.** No door is edited: `ObjectSchema`, `ViewDataSchema`, `FlowSchema` and `registerFlow` refuse exactly what they refused on `main`; `registerFlow` discards the `todos` it now receives. ADR-0087 D2 scopes conversions to "losslessly mappable changes only" and sends the rest to D3, whose own text puts "a structured TODO entry (surface, reason, acceptance criteria) rather than silence" where no declarative migration exists. Refuse-and-list is the ADR's own fate for these shapes.
   - **#23269, choice (b), and its stated reason: RIGHT.** The reason holds on `main`: `migrateStoredMetadata` writes back the read path's own pass (`applyConversionsToStoredItem`, and for a flow row the engine's `canonicalizeStoredFlow`, which `registerFlow` itself calls), so a stored-row rewrite there is a load-seam D2 and must be lossless; `--from 17` replays the chain over authored sources, never rows. The token to CEL rewrite is not lossless (a token that resolved to nothing becomes a CEL fault on an absent root; a flow variable spelled like a query placeholder used to shadow it), which triage's direction already named. The changeset names the choice. The replaced pin ("a converted row boots and runs" has no row under (b); the CEL-form row is pinned canonical, unlisted and registering) is the right substitution.
   - **#23270: RIGHT.** Two masters need a pick (triage: ⛔ no guessed master); an explicit `required: false` is a contradiction the builder refuses; a required `lookup` turned into a `master_detail` changes delete semantics; no master leaves nothing to convert. The one lossless shape stays the D2 `cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted` and is pinned not listed.
   - **#23271: RIGHT.** No mechanical move exists (a page must carry the `dataSource`; deleting `data` makes the view query its object). The population is unmeasured, so listing rather than closing with evidence is the honest branch the card allowed.

2. **The detectors judge with the doors' own predicates: RIGHT.** cbp: `controlledByParentMasterRefusal` is the one function the refinement now calls. View: `ViewDataSchema.safeParse` on the `data` block, listed only when the parse refuses, with `provider: 'api'` as the pre-filter. Flow: `flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals(node.type, node.config)`, the same judge `validateFlowExpressions` runs on every graph (`collectFlowGraphs`, nested regions included); the detector reaches nested regions through `mapFlowNodeList`. One residual difference, noted not failed: the door judges the parsed node and the detector the stored one; the engine pin and the "agrees with the refusing door" pin show one verdict at the CRUD sites, and the judge normalises the legacy `assignment` shapes itself. Reach: `mapViewPayloads` covers all five stored view spellings, plus `objects[].listViews`; `ObjectSchema` declares no `formViews`, so the D3 entry's "listViews / formViews" wording names nothing the detector misses. Never rewrites: the walk helpers are copy-on-write, every detector returns the same reference, and `reportRefusedStoredShapes`'s result is discarded; pinned with and without a sink.

3. **The moved `controlled_by_parent` predicate is behaviour-equivalent at `ObjectSchema`'s refinement: RIGHT.** Same two early returns (other sharing model; non-object `fields`), the same `masters` filter (`type === 'master_detail' && required === true`), the same two issues (`path: ['fields']` for more than one required master, `path: ['sharingModel']` otherwise), the same `found` list in the same order (`masterDetails` is the old `optionalMasters` filter), and the message strings are byte-identical to the inline ones. The `shape` classification is added for the listing only and never reaches the issue.

4. **Keeping the detectors out of `registry.ts`: RIGHT.** A D2 entry is projected as a lossless conversion applied at load (ADR-0087 D2; `spec-changes.json`); a TODO-only entry would publish a false lossless claim. The D2 ledger `conversions/registry.ts` (tracked) is untouched; the D3 ledger changes are prose only (one sentence on three entries' `acceptanceCriteria`), projected in memory by `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide`; `spec-changes.json` and the migrations `registry.ts` are gitignored and generated, so no committed projection changes. The id pin in `refused-shapes.test.ts` (each id is a step-18 D3 entry, never a conversion id) binds the two lists.

5. **`@objectstack/spec` public surface: no export name changes (RIGHT), one published-output widening.** `refused-shapes.ts` and `controlled-by-parent-master.ts` are not re-exported (`conversions/index.ts` and `data/index.ts` unchanged; `object.zod.ts` imports the predicate and re-exports nothing), consistent with #23272 staying its own card. What does widen: the domain of the published `ConversionTodoNotice.conversionId` (a `MetadataConversion.id` on `main`; now also a D3 entry id), and `ApplyConversionsOptions.onTodo` now also fires the refused-shape TODOs. No consumer breaks: the only sink callers are `convertStoredItemDetailed` and now `canonicalizeStoredFlow`, and the renderer prints the id as text, resolving nothing against `ALL_CONVERSIONS` for a TODO. The widening is named in the changeset's wiring paragraph. Cost note, not a contract change: `canonicalizeStoredFlow` always passes a sink now, so every `registerFlow` runs the three detectors over `{ flows: [...] }` (two find nothing there; the flow judge runs once more).

6. **`@objectstack/service-automation` public surface: WIDENED, and not declared.** `AutomationEngine` is exported from the `.` entry; `canonicalizeStoredFlow`'s return type gains `todos: ConversionTodoNotice[]`. By the Clause-② criterion (the public surface is what the built entry declarations reach: re-export names plus every type reachable through props, parameters and return types; widening it, however small, is Clause-②) this is an enlargement of a published package's surface. The PR body says only that the spec's surface is unchanged. See ②.

7. **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` public surface: WIDENED, and not declared.** The exported `StoredFlowCanonicalization` gains `todos?`, which also widens the accept-set of `migrateStoredMetadata({ canonicalizeFlow })`. See ②.

8. **The seat's question (ACCEPT `6152456700`): the published `IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow` contract MUST declare `todos`. Leaving it undeclared is WRONG.**
   - Contract-first (Prime Directive #12): `packages/spec` is the one contract between the two ends we own, and a consumer never tolerates an undeclared dialect with a `??` fallback. `metadata-protocol` now reads `flowResult.todos ?? []`, a member the published contract never promises, through its own structural `StoredFlowCanonicalization`. That type exists (#4454 / #4498) to state "the contract it consumes" structurally, and until this head every member it named was a member the contract declares; after this head the consumer reads past the contract.
   - The contract's own docblock says the method is on the contract because of `os migrate meta --stored` ("the reason this is on the contract rather than only on the implementation"). The stored pass now depends on a fifth output the contract does not name. An implementation conforming to the published contract (the engine `implements IAutomationService`; the method is optional on it) may omit `todos`, and the preview then silently reverts to the pre-PR silence this family exists to end, with the `??` hiding it. That is Prime Directive #10's "declared is not enforced" in reverse: consumed is not declared, while the docs row and three D3 sentences advertise a listing only `AutomationEngine` delivers.
   - The repo's precedent for a member read across this seam is #4127 (pinned in `packages/runtime/src/domain-handler-registry.test.ts`): the dispatcher read `getFlowRuntimeStates` through an inline cast that omitted fields and probed a non-contract `trigger`; the fix declared the member on `IAutomationService` and read through the contract type ("A service that grows one must not be preferred over the contract method"). The #4498 structural resolver in `metadata-protocol` is tolerated because it restates the contract, not because it may exceed it.
   - The fix is one additive optional output on the contract, the sibling of `notices` and `conflicts`: `todos?: ConversionTodoNotice[]`, with a one-sentence docblock, matching `StoredFlowCanonicalization.todos?`. Then the `?? []` reads a contract-declared optional, which is conformance, not tolerance. Optional, not required, so no implementer narrows. That is `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and spec `minor`.

9. **The edited skip reason in `protocol.ts` and the three D3 sentences: TRUE.** The skip reason: a TODO-only row persists nothing and is served as stored (identity test on `storable === body`), and every TODO source on `main` (five `reportTodo` sites) and the three new detectors end the reason with a "Left as stored, ..." sentence, so "each TODO says what that leaves it doing" holds across the family; the dropped "keeps loading unchanged" would indeed have been false for a refused flow. The D3 sentences: "lists each such row as a TODO under this entry's id ... and rewrites none of them" is pinned (ids are D3 ids; `--apply` writes 0; `storedMigrationClean` stays true; `historyRows` empty); "before the upgrade and after it" is the same pass on either side of `--apply`; the fates named (an object registers under `[metadata_spec_invalid]` and derives no master, reads denied and writes 422; a view registers under the same marker and its next save is refused with 422; a flow is not registered at boot and never runs) match `loadMetaFromDb` ("Registered anyway ... `saveMetaItem` rejects new writes (422)"), #23270's measurement and the engine's cold-boot refusal; the view sentence's "showing the request URL and method and withholding every other request key" matches `describeApiBinding` and is pinned on a `Bearer` header. The docs row in `cli.mdx` restates the same fates.

10. **The three packages outside the claim's surface, each named: RIGHT to fix at the producer.** The CLI threads no `canonicalizeFlow` (#4498: the protocol resolves the engine from the kernel's service table itself), so a flow row's TODOs can only come from `canonicalizeStoredFlow`; the STOP path (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta*`) was not needed since the CLI renders `formatStoredMigrationReport`. What this deviation did not carry is the consequence in items 6 to 8.

### ② Semver level

**The changeset `.changeset/23269-v18-stored-row-fates.md` (`patch` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`; `Clause-②: no`) does not match what the diff publishes. FAIL.**

- `@objectstack/service-automation`: `patch` is WRONG. `AutomationEngine.canonicalizeStoredFlow`'s published return type gains `todos`; the method itself entered the package as a 17.0.0 Minor Change. Precedent: `.changeset/23178-settings-auth-gate.md` (`service-settings` `minor`, "an optional `authGate` on the exported `SettingsContext` widens the public surface"); `.changeset/pre/15195-plugin-auth-default-organization-boot-invariant.md` (`plugin-auth` `minor` for optional members on an exported result). Level: `minor`.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: `patch` is WRONG. The exported `StoredFlowCanonicalization` gains `todos?`. Precedent: `.changeset/pre/15204-s6b2-declared-permission-seeders.md` (`metadata-protocol` `minor` for the optional `declared?` argument of `UninstallCleanup`). Level: `minor`.
- `@objectstack/spec`: with the contract declaration ① item 8 requires, `minor`; the `conversionId` domain widening (① item 5) rides the same line.
- **`Clause-②: no` is WRONG** on the PR body and the changeset. Triage's `no` was predicated on "stored v17 rows are converted into what the v18 doors already accept, or refused and listed; nothing widens", which is true of every accept-set at the doors and false of the public surface the chosen wiring adds (two published packages now, three with the contract fix). Per `lanes/spec.md` ("widening an accept-set or enlarging a public surface, however small, is Clause-②") and `landing-operations.md` (a wrong `no` is an auditable false declaration), the line must read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` naming the three members: `IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow(...).todos?`, `AutomationEngine.canonicalizeStoredFlow(...).todos`, `StoredFlowCanonicalization.todos?`. The `(widening)` arm is right; nothing narrows. The claim's `Clause-②: no` on the three cards was the prediction; the diff is the fact.
- `skip-changeset` does not apply (a changeset exists and the packages publish); no breaking changeset, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed; the FROM to TO text is not owed (nothing an author writes is removed or renamed).
- `Check Changeset` is green because it reads the line's presence and spelling, not its truth; per `execution-duties.md` the contract review is the compensating control for a self-declared direction until a mechanical widening gate lands. This record is that control.

**Patch round, three edits, no behaviour change:** (a) declare `todos?: ConversionTodoNotice[]` on `IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow`'s return in `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` with its docblock sentence, and regenerate whatever `check:generated` proves stale on the built tree; (b) rewrite the changeset to `minor` for all three packages with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and the three members named; (c) the same `Clause-②` line on the PR body. The PR body's "the published `IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow` contract type is not edited" sentence then goes.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every deviation and out-of-scope entry in report `6152379792`, answered or escalated:

- **Deviation 1, file surface (`engine.ts`, `protocol.ts`, `stored-migration.ts`, one docs row):** answered in ① item 10; accepted by the seat in `6152456700`. Its unnamed consequence is ② (two published surfaces moved).
- **Deviation 2, Zone 3 route (detectors beside the entries, keyed by D3 id):** right. Entry files are text-concatenated into the gitignored migrations `registry.ts` with their imports dropped, so an entry cannot carry code; the id pin binds detector to entry. Answered.
- **Deviation 3, #23269 reach (every `flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals` site, not only CRUD filters):** right. The D3 entry is one retirement, `registerFlow` refuses every one of its sites alike, and filtering the one judge would re-create the silence for the other sites. Bounded in-place; answered.
- **Deviation 4, pin substitution under (b):** right; answered in ① item 1.
- **Deviation 5, the skip-reason sentence:** true across all eight TODO sources; answered in ① item 9.
- **Deviation 6, `test:repo` NOT MEASURED as a whole:** the narrowing (35 files) and the head's `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are green; Test Core 1 to 6 were `in_progress` at this record's write. A FAIL record enqueues nothing, so the open shards are reported, not assumed; the patch round's head carries its own runs.
- **Deviation 7, commit trailers:** process, not contract; not judged here.
- **Deviation 8, zero label writes:** right.
- **Out-of-scope 1 (a refused flow served `active` after cold boot):** escalated as #23316 by the seat; right not to change the runtime here.
- **Out-of-scope 2 and 3 (page components binding the retired API source; `registerFlow`'s other refusals):** escalated as #23317 by the seat. Right: the view entry's `surface` is the view-level data source, so the preview's scope follows the entry; the general shape is the stored pass running `registerFlow`'s whole validation, which is a card, not this PR.
- **Out-of-scope 4 (`IAutomationService` and `todos`):** answered in ① item 8 and ②: the contract must declare it. Not escalated to a card; it is this PR's patch round, since the consumer already reads the member and the only missing piece is the declaration and the level.
- **Acceptance note (hotcrm's 19 flow files at `0f84c9c` carrying the #23269 shape):** a producer population the listing will now name; carrier is hotcrm's next pin bump. Fine as a note.
- `open_questions`: none in the report.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23269-v18-stored-row-fates`
Reviewed-by: `session_01BRQ9Mp1yH7R1az6MaUM18H`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `086d6f1adca2add2f9d36ca75ec33b85c6c72786`
Local-runs: none

Second-round record on the patch round answering FAIL record `6152721854` (head `af10b608d`). Read: the dev's round report `6154171651` on #23269 and every comment on the three cards and the PR; PR #23315 title, body (as edited for this round) and file list; the net diff `origin/main...086d6f1ad` (merge base `404fc477e`: 18 files, +1097 / -61, matching the report); the round's own commits (`331fa99bb`, a merge of `origin/main`, then `086d6f1ad`: 3 files, +25 / -9); `origin/main` for the contract, the spec's committed projections, `content/docs`, `clause2-line.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`; the repository's merge settings; the head's check-runs at 20:10Z.

**Check-runs on the head at 20:10Z: 48 runs, 41 success, 7 skipped, 0 failed, 0 in progress.** Test Core 1 to 6 (the six shards open at the first record), `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check` (the job that runs every generated-artifact gate, `check:api-surface` and `check:docs` among them), all four `Type Check ·` legs, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, both `Check Changeset` runs, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness` and the claim guards are green. The duplicates are the `pull_request` edited re-runs after the body edit, all green.

### ① Derived judgments

**Scope of this round, verified on the diff:** `git diff --stat af10b608d 086d6f1ad` over the 15 first-round files is empty, so no door, detector, predicate, pin or D3 entry moved since record `6152721854`. The round is exactly the three files the report names. Items 1 to 5, 9 and 10 of `6152721854` ① therefore stand unchanged and are carried forward by reference: one fate per card under triage's rule and ADR-0087 (D2 lossless only, D3's structured TODO otherwise), #23269's choice (b) and its reason, the doors' own predicates in the detectors, the behaviour-equivalent `controlled_by_parent` predicate, the detectors kept out of `registry.ts` with no committed projection changed, the spec export names unchanged, the true skip reason and D3 sentences, and the producer-side fix outside the claim's surface. Items 6, 7 and 8 of that record were the FAIL carriers; this round resolves each:

1. **Item 8, the contract (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`): RESOLVED, RIGHT.** `IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow`'s return declares `todos?: ConversionTodoNotice[]`, optional, the sibling of `notices` and `conflicts`, with a type-only import and a one-sentence docblock; the `@returns` line gains "and (`todos`) the sites left as stored for want of a lossless rewrite". Docblock true: those are exactly the sites the engine collects through `onTodo` (a value slot carrying a `{…}` token among them, which `registerFlow` refuses although the parse accepts it), the stored pass lists them, and absent reads as none (`flowResult.todos ?? []`). Optional is the right arm: the engine's required `todos: ConversionTodoNotice[]` is assignable to it, so `AutomationEngine implements IAutomationService` holds, and no second implementer narrows. The `?? []` in `protocol.ts` now reads a contract-declared optional member, which is conformance, not tolerance (Prime Directive #12 satisfied; the #4127 precedent followed: the member read across the seam is declared on `IAutomationService`). `StoredFlowCanonicalization.todos?`'s docblock now says it restates that member: true, and the structural type is again a subset restatement of the contract's declared outputs. The `#23269` citation sits in TSDoc, not a runtime string, and no author-facing page projects this method (`content/docs` never names it), so the no-tracker-number rule for runtime strings is not touched.

2. **Generated projections: RIGHT that nothing moved.** The spec's committed artifacts record `IAutomationService` by export name only (`api-surface/contracts.json`, `export-origins/contracts.json`); no committed projection names `canonicalizeStoredFlow` or any member, there is no `declaration-map/contracts.json`, `json-schema.manifest` and `authorable-surface` carry schemas not contracts, and `content/docs` never mentions the method or `StoredFlowCanonicalization`. The head's `TypeScript Type Check` job is green, and it reds on any stale artifact, so the dev's `check:generated` "nothing regenerated" reading is confirmed by the gate, not only by the report.

3. **Items 6 and 7, the two service packages' public surfaces: now DECLARED, RIGHT.** `AutomationEngine.canonicalizeStoredFlow(...).todos` (`@objectstack/service-automation`) and `StoredFlowCanonicalization.todos?` (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`) are named in the changeset's `Clause-②` line and its wiring paragraph, and in the PR body's new "Public surface" section, together with the `ConversionTodoNotice.conversionId` domain widening and the `onTodo` sink now receiving refused-shape TODOs.
